NaSO2Ph Induced Exclusive Isomerization of 1,2-Allenyl  
Sulfoxides to 2-Alkynylic Phenyl Sulfoxides 
FU, Chun-Linga(傅春玲)    MA, Sheng-Ming *,a,b,†(麻生明) 
a Laboratory of Molecular Recognition and Synthesis, Department of Chemistry, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, 
Zhejiang 310027, China  
b State Key Laboratory of Organometallic Chemistry, Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of 
Sciences, Shanghai 200032, China 
The clean isomerization of 1,2-allenyl sulfoxides in the presence of NaSO 2Ph afforded 2-alkynylic phenyl sul-
foxides in good yields and selectivities. Although strong base-catalyzed isomerization of allenes to alkynes is 
known, the mechanism for the current reaction is interesting for the obvious reason that NaSO2Ph is a weak base. 
Keywords  1,2-allenyl sulfoxide, isomerization, 2-alkynic phenyl sulfoxide. 
 
Allenes are a class of compounds with unique reac-
tivity.1 Although these compounds had been considered 
highly unstable for a long period of time, 2 recently 
much attention has been paid to the chemistry of allenes. 
This has even become a hot current research area in or-
ganic chemistry.
3    
Heteroatom-substituted allenes have shown excellent 
regio- and stereo-selectivity in halohydroxylation reac-
tions.
4,5 We observed that the stereochemistry of halo-
hydroxylation of allenyl sulfides is different from that of 
allenyl sulfoxides. Actually 1,2-allenyl sulfoxides are a 
class of allenes, which can undergo both electrophilic 
addition and nucleophilic addition. Due to the weak 
electron-withdrawing ability of the sulfoxides, AlCl
3 
was used as a mediator to promote the hydrohalogena-
tion of 1,2-allenyl sulfoxides.
6 Continuing our study on 
the nucleophilic addition reaction of 1,2-allenyl sulfox-
ides, we wish to report here the NaSO
2Ph-mediated 
clean isomerization of 1,2-allenyl sulfoxides to 
propargyl sulfoxides. 
Initially we tested the reaction of 1,2-butadienyl 
sulfoxide 1a with NaSO
2Ph in MeCN in order to pre-
pare 2a. To our surprise instead of the nucleophilic con-
jugate addition product 2a, we observed that 2-butynyl 
phenyl sulfoxide 3a was formed as the only product. 
With 2 equiv. of NaSO2Ph 3a was isolated in 82% yield 
(Scheme 1). The reaction could proceed with 10 mol% 
of NaSO
2Ph affording 3a in 74% yield. 
Although there have been many reports on the clean 
isomerization from alkynes to allenes, 7-9 those on the 
isomerization of allenes to alkynes are quite limited. 10 
Thus, we studied this reaction in detail. The results of 
solvent effect shown in Table 1 indicate that acetonitrile 
Scheme 1

Yield of 3a/% 74 74 75 76  82 
 
is the best solvent. 
Table 2 lists some typical examples of this isomeri-
zation. It should be noted that (1) the reaction is general 
for 3-monosubstituted 1,2-allylic sulfoxides. (2) The 
yields range from moderate to good. (3) The conversion 
is complete since no starting 1 was recovered after the 
time specified in Table 2. 
Strong base-catalyzed isomerization reaction of al-
lenes to alkynes has been well documented in litera-
ture,
10 with the mechanism shown in Scheme 2. It is 
quite interesting to note that NaSO 2Ph is a weak base, 
which may not be able to deprotonate the starting mate-
rial 1 in the current transformation. Thus, the mecha-
nism is a still a puzzle to us. 
In conclusion, a clean conversion of allenes to al-
kynes has been observed. Compared to potassium 
3-aminopropylamide or N-methylbutylamide,

tically interesting. Further study in this area is being 
conducted in our laboratory. 
Experimental  
The starting materials  1 were prepared according to 
the known procedure.11 
Typical procedure  
A solution of 1a (71.6 mg, 0.4 mmol) and NaSO 2Ph 
(131.2 mg, 0.8 mmol) in 2 mL of MeCN was stirred at 
16 ℃ for 6 h. The mixture was quenched with 5 mL of 
water, extracted with diethyl ether (25 mL ×3), washed 
with brine, and dried over anhydrous Na 2SO4. Evapora-
tion and column chromatography on silica gel (petro-
leum ether/ethyl acetate＝3∶1, V∶V) afforded 59.3 mg 
(83%) of 2-butynyl phenyl sulfoxide (3a).
